medical_notes: The title claims stem-cell reactivation, cancer starving and fat burning from a coffee additive, and the image pairs the pouring oil with a cancer-looking cell render without any qualifier.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS
text: ADD THIS to / your COFFEE [bottle label: ORGANIC MCT OIL, PURE & NATURAL]
scene: A cartoon older woman with curly white hair, wire glasses, a blue-and-orange zigzag sweater, a necklace and a ring tilts an amber dropper bottle labelled ORGANIC MCT OIL over a white mug of coffee; two drops fall toward the cup and a spoon rests in it. The left half is a glowing blue microscope-style render of translucent cells, the nearest with a red-brown nucleus, fading into a black right background. A red curved arrow leaves the COFFEE bar and points at the bottle.
mechanism: An imperative headline with the unnamed ingredient shown in a hand pouring it into a cup, plus a cell image that suggests a health effect.
composition: The headline stacks across the top-left two-thirds, the large cell sits lower left, and the woman fills the right third with the bottle and mug at her lower centre. The red arrow bridges text and bottle, so the path runs headline, arrow, bottle, cup, while the cell and the woman pull from opposite sides.
typography: Five words on two lines in white heavy sans with a black outline; COFFEE sits in a red rectangle, ADD THIS is the largest line, and 'to' and 'your' are smaller lower-case words. Everything survives at 160x90 except the bottle label. The title's stem cell, cancer and fat claims are absent from the lettering.
colors: Cool electric blue cells against a black right side, with white text and a saturated red label bar and arrow as the only hot accents. The woman's warm skin and white curls separate cleanly from the black, and the red nucleus in the cell echoes the red bar at the other end of the arrow.
psychology: The woman looks down at the pour with a closed-mouth smile and relaxed shoulders, a calm domestic gesture; white hair and glasses signal her age. The red-nucleus cell is a lab-style cue with no stated outcome.
partnership: The words 'add this to your coffee' restate the title's opening, the bottle label answers what THIS is, and the cell hints at the title's cell and cancer claims without stating them. The three outcome claims in the title are not in the image, so the title carries them alone.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: ADD THIS to your first, the red COFFEE bar and arrow second, then the woman and bottle, with the glowing cell last.
art: A soft-shaded cartoon woman is placed over a photoreal cell render, so two rendering styles share one frame. The membrane texture and glow are detailed; the bottle label is legible only at native size. Dropper, drops and spoon are coherent and no anatomy fault is visible.
strength: Headline, arrow and pour gesture form a tight sequence that tells the viewer to do one specific thing to a coffee cup.
weakness: The photoreal cell and the cartoon woman are different rendering styles, and the cell fills a large area without connecting to the pour.
bottleneck: The oil on the bottle and the cell on the left have no visible link, so the benefit rests on the title rather than the picture.
action: Hypothesis: shrink the large cell to a small icon beside the cup to test whether the pour gesture reads faster with less competing left-side imagery.
mechanism_secondary: cell imagery implying a biological effect
counterexample: Seq 3 is a plain talking-head clip with no graphic claim, where this frame stacks headline, arrow, bottle and cell render.
hero_object: MCT oil dropper bottle over coffee mug

medical_notes: The frame warns about three named prescription antihypertensives and presents a fourth as the better choice beside a pharmacist badge, packaging that reads as drug-switching advice without context.

text: SENIORS MUST KNOW THIS! / IF YOU'RE TAKING / VALSARTAN, METOPROLOL / OR LOSARTAN... / WATCH OUT! / AMLODIPINE / COULD BE THE BETTER CHOICE! [warning triangle icon; name badge: DR. TAVINGHI PHARMACIST]
scene: A woman with long dark wavy hair in green scrubs and a name badge reading DR. TAVINGHI PHARMACIST points her index finger at the text with a slight closed-mouth smile. A glowing yellow heartbeat line crosses the golden backdrop behind her, an amber pill bottle with yellow capsules and a white bottle stand at lower centre, and a blister pack of six white tablets lies across the bottom. A yellow warning triangle with an exclamation mark sits at the top right.
mechanism: A named-drug alert with an authority figure pointing at it: the viewer is told to watch out for three prescriptions and then handed a preferred alternative.
composition: Text takes the left two-thirds in stacked bands: a navy headline strip, yellow and white drug lines, a red brush-stroke WATCH OUT bar and a navy AMLODIPINE box. The woman fills the right third from head to hip, with the finger and pill bottles at the junction. With five banded tiers and about nine distinct elements, nothing owns the frame.
typography: Nineteen words across seven text lines in white and yellow heavy capitals, with WATCH OUT! reversed on a red brush bar. The three drug names stay readable at 160x90, but the AMLODIPINE sub-line and the badge do not. The drug names repeat the title's list, and the thumbnail adds a recommendation the title does not make.
colors: Deep navy, black and a golden-yellow glow carry white and yellow lettering, with a red brush bar and a yellow hazard triangle as the alarm accents. The green scrubs are the only cool mid-tone against the gold, and the strongest contrast sits on the red-and-white WATCH OUT bar.
psychology: The woman holds a direct gaze, a slight smile and an outstretched pointing finger, an instructing posture, and the scrubs and pharmacist badge add authority cues. The red bar and hazard triangle add alarm while her expression stays calm.
partnership: The title lists four blood-pressure drugs and says doctors will not tell the viewer; the thumbnail flags three of them with WATCH OUT and singles out the fourth as the better choice. The badge name differs from the channel name supplied for this video, which a viewer cannot reconcile from the frame.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: SENIORS MUST KNOW THIS first, the yellow IF YOU'RE TAKING block second, the red WATCH OUT bar third, then the pointing hand, with AMLODIPINE last.
art: A photoreal woman is cut out cleanly against a graphic gold glow, with consistent lighting on face and scrubs. The pill bottles and the blister pack are coherent, and no visible artefact appears; the heartbeat line passes behind her shoulder without overlap errors.
strength: The red WATCH OUT bar and hazard triangle make an unmistakable alert, and the named drugs speak directly to people on those prescriptions.
weakness: Seven text lines and five banded tiers compete, and the AMLODIPINE sub-line and name badge are unreadable at phone size.
bottleneck: No single element wins the frame, so the first read depends on the viewer already taking one of the named drugs.
action: Hypothesis: cut the layout to the headline strip, the WATCH OUT bar and one drug name to test whether a single-claim frame beats the five-tier stack.
counterexample: Seq 18 uses one three-word question and a single huge orange shape, where this frame carries nineteen words.
expression_label: slight closed-mouth smile with direct gaze and pointing finger
hero_object: amlodipine banner with pill bottles and blister pack

text: BUT YES, IT REALLY / CAN BE THAT SIMPLE / Leslie Kernisan, MD MPH [footer web address: BetterHealthWhileAging.net]
scene: A vertical video frame sits centred in the 16:9 canvas with blurred teal-grey bars on either side. In it a woman with dark curly hair, hoop earrings and a black jacket looks into the camera with a faint closed-mouth smile, and a blue desk microphone rises into the lower edge. A mint caption box at the top holds the headline, a lower-third strip carries the speaker's name and credentials, and a mint footer bar carries a small web address.
mechanism: A talking-head clip with a credential strip and a reassurance caption; the image relies on the speaker's presence rather than a visual proposition.
composition: The speaker's face sits slightly above centre of the vertical column, with the caption box above her hair and the name strip across her chest. The column spans just under a third of the canvas width, so the rest of the frame is blurred padding.
typography: Twelve words in two small text items: a two-line black caption in a mint box and a one-line name strip, plus a footer address too small to read. At 160x90 both collapse into tiny marks, and the wording mentions neither B12 nor geriatrics.
colors: Muted sage green and grey-teal side bars, a beige wall, a black jacket and mint caption blocks that echo the bars. Saturation is low, and the only strong contrast is black text on mint and the dark jacket against the wall.
psychology: A direct gaze, slightly raised brows and a faint closed-mouth smile with a desk microphone in view read as a calm one-person explainer, and the printed MD MPH credential adds an authority cue.
partnership: The title promises geriatrician recommendations on B12 deficiency, but the caption is a mid-sentence fragment naming no nutrient and the credential carries no specialty. The 'it really can be that simple' wording raises an unanswered question about what is simple.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the caption box at the top first, then the face, then the name strip, with the blurred side bars skipped.
art: A real video still with soft indoor light, a plain wall and a visible microphone. The side bars are a blurred fill that letterboxes the vertical clip, and the caption boxes are flat-colour overlays.
strength: A real human face with a printed credential on a plain background reads as a straightforward expert clip.
weakness: The caption is a mid-sentence fragment with no topic word, so nothing on the frame names B12 or the problem.
bottleneck: At phone size the text is unreadable and the face sits in a narrow centre column, which leaves no message beyond a person.
action: Hypothesis: replace the subtitle fragment with a three-word topic caption at twice the type size to test whether a named topic improves the first-glance read.
counterexample: Seq 1 fills the full 16:9 canvas with a large headline and glowing imagery, where this frame leaves two-thirds as blurred side bars.
expression_label: faint closed-mouth smile with direct gaze

scene: A giant purple octopus with narrowed, heavy-lidded eyes, long lashes and drawn-down brows looms over a smaller orange octopus at the lower left. The orange one has bulging bloodshot eyes, an open mouth showing teeth and tongue, blue tears and sweat drops, and short tremor lines around its body. A strip of blue water runs along the bottom and a thin black curved arrow at the upper left points down at the orange octopus.
mechanism: A consequence statement paired with a predatory-looking giant and a terrified small animal, so the cost of being an octopus is pictured instead of described.
composition: The purple body fills the centre and top with tentacles reaching the right edge, the orange octopus sits low left, and the two-line text sits upper right on white. The scale contrast sets a diagonal from the glaring eyes down to the screaming face.
typography: Four words on two lines in black: a thin hand-lettered It Dies above heavy TO MATE, which stands roughly twice the height of the first line. TO MATE survives at 160x90 and It Dies is thinner but still legible. The words name a cause the title's complaint leaves out.
colors: Violet and orange sit near opposite points on the wheel, so the two octopuses separate sharply against the white ground; blue water and tears add a small cool accent. Black outlines and black type keep every edge crisp.
psychology: The large octopus shows a glare under lowered lids, while the small one shows wide eyes, an open mouth and tears; the pair reads as looming-over versus cowering through exaggerated cartoon expression. No person appears.
partnership: The title asks why being born an octopus is bad, and the text answers in four words with a death-in-mating claim that the sobbing small octopus supports. Which octopus 'it' refers to is left ambiguous, which keeps a question open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the screaming orange face first, the big purple glare second, then TO MATE, with It Dies read last.
art: Clean cartoon linework with flat fills and consistent outline weight; the bloodshot eyes and the suckers are drawn with care. The purple tentacles overlap the orange head coherently, and the white ground keeps the image uncluttered at small size.
strength: A purple giant over a sobbing orange octopus makes the mating-death claim readable before any word is read.
weakness: The thin It Dies line is lighter than TO MATE, and the small black arrow at upper left is easy to miss.
bottleneck: It is unclear which octopus 'it' is, so the claim reads as a general fact more than a pointed story.
action: Hypothesis: thicken It Dies to match TO MATE and enlarge the arrow to test whether the first-read order locks onto the victim.
counterexample: Seq 5 shows one calm stick figure beside a still ship, where this frame stages a violent scale contrast.
expression_label: giant's lowered-lid glare versus small one's open-mouth cry
hero_object: terrified orange octopus beneath a giant purple octopus

scene: A white round-headed stick figure with a thick black outline stands at the left edge with a raised eyebrow, eyes glancing right and a flat mouth, its thin legs cut off at the bottom. Beside it a huge black ship hull streaked with orange-red rust lies on a dark seabed, with upper decks and a small crane above the rail. The background is flat saturated blue.
mechanism: A curiosity question about a famous wreck, delivered as a deadpan stick-figure reaction beside a rusting hull.
composition: RAISE IT? spans the full width across the top third, with the figure at left and the wreck along the lower right two-thirds as the larger secondary mass. The figure's sideways glance leads toward the ship, and the empty blue band between text and ship separates the two.
typography: Two words in giant yellow capitals with a thick black outline and a question mark, spanning almost the whole frame width and fully legible at 160x90. The wording omits the ship's name, which only the title supplies.
colors: Saturated cobalt blue with yellow lettering, black hull and orange-red rust, so the three hues are well separated; the white head is the lightest point in the frame. Yellow on blue is the highest-contrast pair present.
psychology: The flat mouth, raised brow and sideways glance show doubt, and the rusted wreck adds a decay and abandonment cue. The tone is deadpan and not alarmed.
partnership: RAISE IT? poses the title's action as a question and the image fills in the object, a rusted wreck, so the two share one thought. The answer, why nobody has done it, stays open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow RAISE IT? first, the white stick-figure head second, then the rusted hull, reading left to right.
art: A deliberately simple stick figure stands beside a more detailed, textured ship, so the two rendering levels differ. The rust streaks run consistently down the hull and a seabed shadow grounds the ship, and the flat blue adds no clutter.
strength: Two giant words and one rusted wreck pose a single clear question in a flat-colour layout.
weakness: The ship is not named in the text, so a viewer who does not recognise the wreck sees only a rusty hull.
bottleneck: The stick figure's blank stare is the only emotional cue, so interest rests on recognising the ship.
action: Hypothesis: add a small line reading TITANIC under RAISE IT? to test whether naming the ship helps viewers who do not recognise the hull.
counterexample: Seq 24 packs five faces and a long headline into the same canvas, where this frame holds one figure and two words.

scene: A cartoon man with a smooth pale face, half-lidded eyes and a closed-mouth smile walks past an open elevator in a navy suit and blue tie, with a lanyard ID card in one hand and a brown briefcase in the other. Inside the elevator, five coworkers in dark suits and lanyards cheer and clap under falling confetti, and the central one raises both fists. A red curved arrow from under the headline points at the walking man's head.
mechanism: An isolated exit set against a group celebration, with the headline stating that the group did not join.
composition: NOBODY FOLLOWED. fills the upper left, the walking man stands left of centre at near full height, and the lit elevator frames the cheering group in the right third. The arrow bridges text and head, and the orange elevator interior is a bright box that competes with the man.
typography: Two words on two lines in white heavy capitals with a black outline and a full stop, in the upper left; both are fully readable at 160x90. The text adds the twist that the title's 'You Got Out' only implies.
colors: Warm orange interior and confetti inside the elevator against cool grey tiles and a desaturated hall, with the navy suit and red arrow as the high-contrast pieces. The man's pale face is the lightest area in his half of the frame.
psychology: Half-lidded eyes and a closed-mouth smile on the walker contrast with open-mouthed laughter and raised fists in the elevator, so the crowd looks joyful while he looks composed. The ID lanyard held in his hand reads as a work badge carried out.
partnership: The title says everyone got promoted and 'you' got out; the thumbnail turns that into one man leaving while a crowd celebrates. The text adds that no one joined him, and whether leaving was a win or a loss is left for the video.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: NOBODY FOLLOWED. first, the red arrow to the man's face, then the cheering elevator group, then the briefcase and badge.
art: Smooth digital cartoon with soft lighting; the walker's blank white face is flatter than his shaded suit, and the elevator door and tiled floor keep a consistent perspective. Confetti and the five coworkers' faces are legible at native size but blur at 160x90.
strength: A lone walker beside a cheering lift gives a one-glance contrast of 'out' versus 'promoted'.
weakness: The bright, busy elevator box pulls attention away from the walker's face.
bottleneck: The walker's expression is neutral, so it is unclear whether leaving reads as a win or a loss.
action: Hypothesis: reduce the elevator crowd to two figures and mute the orange glow to test whether the walker's face holds focus better.
counterexample: Seq 7 is one huge face on white with a verdict line, where this frame tells a two-zone story.
hero_object: walking man with ID lanyard beside cheering elevator

scene: A cartoon man with slicked-back brown hair, forehead and cheek creases, thick angled brows, red irises and a lopsided grin showing a grey line of teeth fills the left half. He wears a red suit jacket, white shirt and red tie. A thin hand-drawn black arrow curves from the text up toward the top of his head.
mechanism: A second-person accusation attached to a villain portrait, which casts the viewer as the character.
composition: The face and shoulders take the left 55 percent of the frame, the two-line text column sits on the right, and open white space isolates the text. The arrow runs from the text to the hairline and closes a simple two-part loop.
typography: Four words on two lines in thin hand-style black lettering, except Evil, which is red; the lines are large and readable at 160x90 though the strokes are lighter than a bold headline. The text delivers a verdict on the viewer that the title's 'ruthless' only hints at.
colors: White ground with a saturated red suit, tie and the single red word, plus a warm tan face and dark brown hair. The red is menace-coded and repeats in the irises and in Evil, while everything else is black or white.
psychology: Lowered, angled brows, red irises, a one-sided grin and a forward-tilted head read as menace, and the red clothing amplifies it. The words 'You Are' put the viewer in the role.
partnership: The title offers a role-play as a ruthless hedge fund CEO; the thumbnail escalates it to a moral verdict with a villain portrait. No hedge-fund imagery appears, so the finance setting comes only from the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red-suited face first, the red word Evil second, then 'You Are', with the arrow pointing back at the head.
art: Clean vector-style cartoon with consistent outlines, shading on the hair and jacket and a crisp cutout on white. Anatomy and the tie knot are coherent, while the hand-drawn arrow uses a looser line style than the polished figure.
strength: A huge menacing face and one red word make the villain role instant to read.
weakness: No finance prop appears, so the portrait could belong to any villain topic.
bottleneck: The title's finance context is missing from the image, so relevance rests on the title.
action: Hypothesis: add a stock-chart screen behind the shoulder to test whether a finance cue improves topic clarity without weakening the face.
counterexample: Seq 8 shows a relaxed figure in a warm room with a quiet label, where this frame uses a menacing close-up.
expression_label: angled brows, red irises and one-sided grin

scene: A cartoon man with an oversized cream-coloured round face, a navy cap, a white open-collar shirt and dark trousers sits cross-legged in a brown leather armchair, holding a steaming mug in one hand and a tablet showing a rising green line chart in the other. Behind him a lamp-lit study has a bookshelf, a potted plant and a side table with a notepad and pen. Through a large window at right, a stream of suited commuters with briefcases hurries along a blue-tinted street. A red curved arrow from the white word YOU points at his head.
mechanism: A warm indoor figure set against a hurrying outdoor crowd, with a pointer word that makes the viewer the seated man.
composition: The seated man fills the left half and stands out against the warm room, while the window cuts the frame vertically and the commuters fill the right 45 percent. YOU sits at the top above the lamp, and the red arrow drops to his head, setting a warm-left versus cool-right split.
typography: One word, YOU, in white heavy capitals with a dark outline, small relative to the frame and set above the lamp; it is readable at 160x90 but carries little meaning alone. The title's POV and early-retirement ideas are absent from the lettering.
colors: Amber and brown tones inside the room against desaturated blue-grey outside, making a warm-cool contrast on a vertical split; the red arrow and navy cap are small saturated accents. The man's white shirt and cream face are the brightest area in the room.
psychology: The man has level brows, a small smile and a relaxed crossed-leg posture with a mug, while the commuters' faces are tiny and neutral at a glance. Rest indoors versus hurrying outdoors frames a leisure-versus-commute story.
partnership: YOU labels the seated man as the viewer, while the title supplies the decades-early retirement claim; the scene adds the contrast between his rest and the passing workers. The tablet's rising chart hints at funding without stating a figure.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: YOU and the red arrow first, the man's cap and face second, then the tablet and mug, and finally the commuters through the window.
art: Polished digital cartoon with soft gradient lighting and consistent perspective on the armchair, window and street; the man's blank round head is flatter than his shaded clothing. The commuter crowd is detailed but desaturated, so it recedes at small size.
strength: A warm armchair beside a cold street of hurrying workers states the premise in one glance.
weakness: The word YOU is small and says little, and the props in the room and the crowded window add detail that blurs at phone size.
bottleneck: Nothing in the image indicates the early-retirement age, so the decades-early hook sits in the title alone.
action: Hypothesis: replace YOU with a short line naming the retirement age in large type to test whether a quantified claim strengthens the frame.
counterexample: Seq 10 shows the same relaxed-versus-commuters premise with no text, where this frame adds a pointer word.
hero_object: armchair man with tablet beside commuter window
